decision.what: One entry point = record_lines(file, lines) in page_tools.js: applies each line to the file's live root (if one is warm), then appends it. Its one door is POST /api/item: {path, delta} (verbs, as today) or {path, lines} (raw lines from hooks, LogLine and the browser's page files). One client, core/Item/RecordWriter.js, used by Store (browser) and the hooks/append.mjs (node): posts, and only when the door is down falls back to a raw append that first checks the file's tail for the same line stamped since the post began (no twin). A slow door is waited on, never answered by a blind self-append.
options: Live root catches up on outside growth (replay only new bytes): fixes the cost for every writer but keeps many writers; kept as a later guard, not the design
Move the door to each project's dev server now (F1): ask-first per the brief; RecordWriter.entry() is the one line that moves

findings.text: Ask 1 says every write to a record file goes through the entry point, but Servex's own direct appends to task and session records still skip it and leave the live root stale: `Servex/agents/Agents.js:1082`, `:1736`, `:2280`, `:2319`, `Servex/Lifecycle.js:126`, `Servex/WorktreeWatch.js:290`. They run inside Servex, so routing them to `record_lines` is cheap. If they stay out, `core/Item/doc/one-writer.md` "Not routed" must list them, because today it names only line 1 of new sessions.

`core/Item/doc/map.md` is stale. Its "How a change is saved" section (lines 49–60) says a browser change goes `Store.flush` → `FsFile.send` → `Append.js` with no `by` or `ts`, and the map's writer table never names `RecordWriter.js` or `record_lines`. This file is the module's own "every writer" map, so it has to describe the one writer.
`core/Item/doc/architecture.md:49` still says the Store "sends each new line via `FsFile.send`". For record files that path is now only the fallback, behind `RecordWriter.post`.

Ask 4 also requires the integration branch's smoke, but no smoke result is recorded. `proof/` holds `tests.txt` (74 of 77, the same 3 baseline failures) and `replay-compare.txt` (9626 of 9626 the same). `proof/browser-probe.mjs` is there, but none of its output is saved, so a fresh agent cannot confirm that a tab click on the worktree's dev server still saves once. Save the probe's output in `proof/`.

`Server/LogLine.mjs` `append`: when `record_lines` answers `ok: "partly"`, it is not thrown, so `report` says every line was appended even though some were refused. `.claude/hooks/append.mjs` makes the opposite mistake: on a partial refusal it exits 3 with "Not written" after the other lines were written.

`.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs` now makes one HTTP post for each record line on every hook event, with a 3 s timeout (`RecordWriter.write`). When Servex's event loop is held (the crumbs case), every hook can stall for 3 s. Hook latency was not measured.

One twin window remains beyond the same-millisecond limit in `one-writer.md`. Suppose `run_item_now` passes its `already` tail check (`page_tools.js` near the `stamp` change) and is still writing when the tab's 15 s fallback goes through `Append.js`. Both writers then see a tail without the line, and both write it. It is rare, but the doc should name it.

`serve_item` ignores the `by` that `RecordWriter.post` sends with a verb (`page_tools.js`, `serve_item`), and the caller is always `"owner"`. That is right for a tab, but the field does nothing, so a future node caller posting verbs would be stamped as the owner.
`core/Item/doc/one-writer.md` says "RecordWriter.test.mjs (7 checks)", but the file has 9, and the task log says 9/9.

assign.title: core/Item: one writer for record files (build D), ready on worktree/one-writer, not merged
assign.outcome:
Every line bound for a session, task, page or improvements.jsonl now goes through one entry point in Servex (POST /api/item: record_lines for raw lines, run_item for verbs), which applies it to the file's live root and then appends it. Callers use one class, core/Item/RecordWriter.js: the browser Store, the hooks (ledger, naming-guard), append.mjs, LogLine and Servex's own alert and assign lines. The blind 5 s browser self-append is gone; the fallback (when Servex is down, slow or stubbed) checks the file's tail and writes once.

Branch worktree/one-writer at 34fb0294e (locked, NOT merged), url http://one-writer.localhost/ (port 49570).

Tests: one-writer.test 19/19 (two writers: 40 lines, no twin, none lost; a hook write: 1 full replay before, 0 after; fallback once when down, slow, stubbed, late either order), RecordWriter.test 9/9, suite 75 of 78 with the integration's same 3 failures (PromptLines, context-alert, item_tool; item_tool 113 checks, identical single failure). Replay comparison 9,626/9,626 files the same. Smoke: the 43 shared pages identical to the integration's (36 FAIL, 7 ok, same kinds: generated-file 404s in a fresh worktree, text touching its box), no page errors.

Measured, the next item() call after a hook write: voice session v-sq8y7db (8,383 lines) 164 ms -> 16.5 ms; session-e00f55c9 (1,099 lines) 69 ms -> 25 ms.

Review: verdict fix, 9 findings, every one answered (7 fixed, 2 written into one-writer.md as known limits), in commit 34fb0294e and the session log.

F1 (ask first): moving the entry point to each project's dev server is lifting record_lines/serve_item/run_item/live_root into Server/plugins/Item.js and changing RecordWriter.entry(), one line; no caller changes.

Left: about 20 other Servex/Server files still append records directly (no loss; the next item() replays once), filed as the core/Item improvement. Notes: the worktree's Servex/node_modules was installed with npm ci; the main tree's hooks are untouched; the worktree's own dev server keeps rewriting files.jsonl indexes while it runs (machine churn, not work).
